summary: Bernhard Karlgren was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915). He later held posts at Uppsala University (~1915–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. He held academic posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist and religious studies, earning degrees at Brooklyn, NYU, and UCLA, and studying under teachers Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Jonathan A. Silk, later holding posts at Heidelberg University (2015) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, and Franz Bopp. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg and served as professor at the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady, he held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and the Field Museum of Natural History.

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who completed her doctorate at the University of Munich and studied under Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the University of Vienna, and the Alice Boner Foundation.

Betty Heimann was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Strasbourg, Kiel, and Halle under teachers including Georg Simmel, Emil Sieg, and Eugen Hultzsch. She held posts at Halle, Hamburg (1931–1933), London (~1934–1945), and Ceylon (1945–1949).
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was an Indologist and linguist who earned his A.M. and Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Murray B. Emeneau. He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad.

Bhagavan Das was an Indian philosopher and scholar of religion and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University and served as headmaster of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he served as head of the Research Department as attested in 1989.

Bhagwan Dash was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Gujarat Ayurved University, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, where he earned an M.A. and Ph.D., and worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer for the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was a member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1864–1888) and a Fellow at the University of Mumbai.

Bhajagobinda Ghosh was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and an editorial board member for the Bulletin of Tibetology, attested in 1994.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan.
Bhau Daji Lad was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology who studied at Elphinstone College and Grant Medical College (~1845–1850).

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and University of Marburg, and held posts at the University of Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, and Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Claremont Graduate University and studied under Nyanaponika Thera. He was editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States.
